minutes.headline: FY26 budget gap forces deep proposed staff cuts, hitting young grades and special education hardest
minutes.summary: The school committee handled routine business (minutes, grants, a track-and-field warrant article, facility contracts, a competency determination, and a revised superintendent search adding external candidates) before spending most of the meeting on a grim FY26 budget presentation: to meet the town manager's target the district would cut dozens of teaching, paraprofessional, counseling and support positions, with the deepest impact on elementary grades and special education. No budget vote was taken; the committee instead gave feedback, discussed alternative revenue and staffing ideas, and heard extensive public comment expressing alarm about the proposed cuts and frustration with state Chapter 70 funding.

what_happened.line: The superintendent laid out proposed cuts to teaching, paraprofessional and support staff, falling hardest on elementary grades and special education, to meet the town manager's FY26 target; no budget vote was taken.
Even after applying grants, revolving-fund offsets and expense cuts, the revised budget proposal still left a gap against the town's target, according to the presentation.
The committee voted 4 to 1 to approve the district's competency determination.
The committee voted 3 to 1, with one abstention, to approve the high school's program of studies.
The chair will revise the committee's Chapter 70 funding letter and send it to state legislators, the governor and surrounding districts instead of separate resolutions.

why_it_matters: The staffing cuts described would touch elementary classrooms and special education services directly, which residents may notice in class sizes and support before any town meeting vote on the budget itself.
watch_next: Next School Committee meeting: missing January warrants and facilities director hiring status added to the agenda
A joint discussion among the school committee, Council on Aging, facilities director and library on the Kids Kingdom Playground move, before any proposal returns for a vote

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the formal actions taken — nearly every motion, second, and vote tally (grant approval, warrant article, assessment report, LHS program of studies 3-1-1, facilities report, capital contracts, competency determination 4-1, search consultant directive, tabling reports) matches between the two records. The biggest thing to know is that the official minutes are essentially silent on the FY26 budget presentation's actual numbers (level-service total, target-budget gap, proposed cuts, FTE reductions, tuition, utilities, cost drivers, athletics fee) — those figures exist only in our machine-caption-derived minutes and cannot be cross-checked against the official text at all, and one seated committee member (Laura Brzozoski, who spoke and made/seconded multiple motions) is entirely absent from our attendee list.
